items.title: Can robust TSMC earnings help settle AI jitters? By Investing.com
items.author: Senad Karaahmetovic
items.highlights: Investing.com - TSMC posted a $23.59 billion net profit for the third quarter of 2026, a 68.7% year-over-year surge that marked its sixth consecutive record quarter, yet the earnings beat has done little to arrest a deepening selloff across AI-linked semiconductor stocks. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing, the world’s largest contract chipmaker and a foundry supplier to NVIDIA, AMD, and Apple, is the stock most exposed to AI hardware demand: its revenue is tied directly to the volume and complexity of chips ordered by hyperscalers and AI accelerator makers. items.author: Nauman Khan

items.title: TSMC ADRs Jump 2% as Nvidia Extends the Foundry Runway
items.author: Khac Phu Nguyen
items.highlights: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE:TSM), the world's largest contract chipmaker, delivered a tale of two markets Thursday. Taipei shares slipped 0.2%. Hours later, the U.S.-listed ADR jumped approximately 2.0% to $425.97 after Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) projected roughly 70% revenue growth next fiscal year. Taiwan closed before that bombshell. Wall Street did not miss it. TSMC hardly entered the rally empty-handed. July revenue rocketed 44.7% year over year to NT$467.58 billion. First-seven-month revenue climbed 37% to NT$2.872 trillion.
